title: Neural Fingerprints in MEG and fMRI
summary:
Every person has unique patterns of brain activity. Recent research suggests that these patterns may be so individual that they can be used to distinguish people in a way that is similar to a fingerprint. However, it is still unclear how stable these individual patterns are over time, which aspects of brain activity contribute most strongly to this individuality, and whether these patterns are related to psychological characteristics such as attention, resilience, or emotion regulation.

The aim of this study is to investigate individual patterns of brain activity in healthy adults. Brain activity and brain structure will be measured using two non-invasive neuroimaging methods. In addition, participants will complete questionnaires assessing different psychological characteristics.

Participants will take part in a one-time assessment including resting-state brain recordings and magnetic resonance imaging of the brain. The collected data will be used to characterize individual patterns of brain activity and to explore their relationship with psychological characteristics.
conditions: Investigation of individual differences in resting-state brain activity (“neural fingerprints”), including their stability, identifiability, and association with psychological characteristics in healthy adults.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-Healthy adults
-Ability to understand study information and provide informed consent
-Willingness to participate in MEG, MRI, and questionnaire assessments
-No contraindications to MEG or MRI
Exclusion criteria:
-Current neurological or psychiatric disorders that could relevantly affect study participation, participant safety, or interpretation of the acquired data
-Current use of medication that may affect brain activity
-Acute alcohol or recreational drug intoxication at the time of participation
-Contraindications to MEG or MRI, including pacemakers, neurostimulators, insulin pumps, non-MRI-compatible implants, or metallic foreign bodies
-Non-removable metal-containing braces or retainers
-Severe claustrophobia
-Other safety-relevant exclusion criteria according to MEG/MRI safety screening
